about: How tools/rig-fish.py rigs the fish of Cocolalla Lake. Every fish gets the same skeleton: a body, a head in front of it and a tail in four parts. "bends" says where the joints are, as shares of the fish's length from its nose (0) to the end of its tail fin (1): the body runs between the two "body" shares, the head is everything in front of it, and each "tail" share starts the next part of the tail. A fish may give its own "body" or "tail" in place of these. "triangles" is how many triangles each fish is thinned to: Meshy makes about 31,000, and several fish are on screen at once at the lake's heaviest place. The pike keeps more because the monster pike is drawn from it, much bigger.
